title: PolicyAppliedData
description: data of policy.applied (PRD 9.5). The deterministic policy engine opened a gate under a policy (PRD 10.4). Never T3, never below L2. authz is by policy with ref equal to policy_id (EV-06), so the world draws a policy stamp and links it (HR-7); the outbox entry and its outgoing data.transfer carry exactly this authz (OB-01). There is no gate card on this path, so this event records what the engine assessed against the policy's scope: the connector, the destination (an opaque id, never an address), the district of the step, the tier, the undo window, and item pinned to its version (null when there is none). The outbox entry equals it on each (OB-05) and the policy's scope covers it (OB-01), so a redraft, another thread or another connector is a new proposal. L2 is 'instruction is approval' (PRD 10.4, FR-HIL-05): instruction_id is the id of the earlier world.requested (web or mobile_web) or channel.message_in (whatsapp, from the owner's bound number) in this world in which the policy's owner asked for this action on this destination, never an email, and HR-7 links it beside the policy; each instruction is named by at most one policy.applied, so a cancelled send uses it up (OB-01); at L2 the destination is set and the undo window is at least 1 s. At L3 (a standing rule within its limits) instruction_id is null. credits is what this action counts against the policy's daily credit limit (limits.credits, BQ-14): the metered credits of the step whose side effect it is, as known at authz.at (PRD 14.1); the event's own spend stays in the envelope's credits. The engine opens a send only while the policy's actions that UTC day in every world of its owner, this one included, stay within limits.per_day and their credits within limits.credits (OB-01, BQ-52). Recipients stay in the outbox entry, never in an event.
